argument:
CelcomDigi's realised RM141m savings and positive underlying service growth offer a gradual integration-and-income purchase case. Normalised Q2 PAT grew 0.9% and EBIT 3.7%, tempering the reported profit-decline narrative without denying its costs. The vendor-reported 5.42% yield provides potential income compensation if ongoing efficiencies strengthen cash available for distributions.

Statutory H1 CFO was RM1.222bn, not the presentation's differently defined RM2.439bn. Cash after capex and leases was RM445m against RM821m dividends, while borrowings rose to RM14.461bn and cash/deposits were only RM834m. Positive post-lease cash makes improvement feasible, but current payout cannot be called fully covered. At 19.31x trailing earnings, modest growth needs genuine integration delivery. Oversold RSI offers no reversal proof; buying remains conditional on efficiency gains closing the funding gap.
key_points: Realised savings and slightly growing normalised earnings support gradual improvement.
Positive statutory cash persists after capex and leases.
Dividend cash shortfall and rising borrowings require payout/integration discipline.
